target_customer: Website publishers and online merchants who wanted to send browser push notifications to returning visitors
problem: Websites had no cheap way to re-engage visitors who left, since email and RSS had weak engagement. Roost offered push notifications for the web, first through the Safari standard and later Chrome and Firefox.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for publishers and merchants, with a 30 day trial and CMS plugins

founders.name: Tim Varner
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists only Tim Varner and gives no biography. Other databases name additional people but no company source I opened confirms them, so they are left out.

competitors.name: Twitter
competitors.what: Social feed that the YC launch post says Roost wanted to replace for following publishers

competitors.name: RSS readers
competitors.what: Feed readers that the launch post says had failed to win mainstream use

competitors.name: PageMonitor
competitors.what: Browser plug-in for watching pages for changes, contrasted with Roost in the launch post

technical_complexity.rationale: Building on the Safari push standard needed certificate handling and per browser support, with Chrome and Firefox support still promised in mid 2014 per the YC launch post and coverage.

defensibility.rationale: Push became a browser standard open to anyone, so a dashboard and plugins layer was copyable by many vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources I opened. Browsers later opened the standard to all vendors.

market_need_then: Safari had shipped website push with OS X Mavericks and Chrome and Firefox support was announced for the coming months, so a first mover tooling layer had a timing window in 2014 per press coverage of the launch.

branding.domain_note: Used goroost.com rather than the exact .com, per the YC page.
branding.community_and_virality: A 2014 personal blog post and a Zapier integration post showed some developer interest. No fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found no brand coverage. Several unrelated companies share the name Roost, which makes the name confusable.

outcome_analysis: Roost was a first mover in website push notifications in 2014, but the capability was a browser standard that any vendor could wrap. Its funding totals in public databases are small and conflict. The shutdown cause is not public, so no failure factors are asserted.
notes: Company site goroost.com did not resolve in this session. The 2013 seed was raised by Notice Software, the predecessor name per a Crunchbase snippet, and rests on one outlet. The VentureBeat figures come from search snippet text only because the page fetch was rate limited, and they state about 900000 in cumulative seed money from Rocket Ventures, the University of Toledo UTIE and Y Combinator at 125000. The 190000 seed rests on one aggregator. Seedtable lists 400000 over one round and conflicts. Dealroom marks the company closed with no cause. The cause of failure is not public.
